subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "She writes a letter."
options: A letter is wrote by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter is written by her.
A letter writes by her.
explain: Simple present passive = is/am/are + past participle.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "They built this bridge."
options: This bridge is built by them.
This bridge were built by them.
This bridge has built by them.
This bridge was built by them.
explain: Simple past passive = was/were + V3; singular object takes 'was'.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "He will finish the work."
options: The work will finished by him.
The work will be finished by him.
The work will be finish by him.
The work would be finished by him.
explain: Simple future passive = will/shall + be + V3.

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence cannot normally be changed into the passive voice?
options: She sings a song.
He wrote a letter.
The baby sleeps soundly.
They will buy a car.
explain: Intransitive verbs (no object) have no passive.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Who wrote this poem?"
options: By whom was this poem written?
By whom is this poem written?
By whom was this poem wrote?
Whom was this poem written by them?
explain: Who (subject) becomes 'By whom'; past tense needs was + written.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "He does not play cricket."
options: Cricket was not played by him.
Cricket is not play by him.
Cricket does not played by him.
Cricket is not played by him.
explain: 'does not play' → 'is not played'; do/does is dropped.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "She gave me a book."
options: I was gave a book by her.
I were given a book by her.
I was given a book by her.
I am given a book by her.
explain: Simple past: was + given; 'I' takes 'was'.

subject: English
prompt: Which pattern forms the passive of the Present Continuous tense?
options: has/have + been + V3
am/is/are + V3 + being
am/is/are + been + V3
am/is/are + being + V3
explain: Present continuous passive = am/is/are + being + past participle.

subject: English
prompt: Which pattern forms the passive of the Past Continuous tense?
options: was/were + V3 + being
was/were + being + V3
was/were + been + V3
had been + being + V3
explain: Past continuous passive = was/were + being + past participle.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Who is teaching you English?"
options: By whom you are being taught English?
Who is being taught English by you?
By whom is English taught to you?
By whom are you being taught English?
explain: Who → By whom; are you being taught keeps present continuous.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Is she singing a song?"
options: Is a song being sung by her?
Is a song sung by her?
Has a song been sung by her?
Was a song being sung by her?
explain: Is + subject + being + V3 keeps the interrogative present continuous.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: 'They will have finished the work by noon.' Correct verb group?
options: will have being finished
would have been finished
will have been finished
will be finished
explain: Future perfect passive = will have been + past participle.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: 'She has eaten all the mangoes.' → 'All the mangoes ___ eaten by her.'
formula: has/have been + V3 (agrees with new subject)
options: has been
have been
are being
had been
explain: New subject 'mangoes' is plural, so present perfect passive takes 'have been'.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the error: 'The letter had been wrote before I reached.'
options: had been
reached
wrote
before
explain: Passive needs past participle 'written', not the past form 'wrote'.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: 'Who has broken the window?'
options: By who has the window been broken?
Whom has the window been broken?
By whom the window has been broken?
By whom has the window been broken?
explain: 'Who' becomes 'By whom'; question order is retained: has + subject + been + V3.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: 'Had the police caught the thief?'
options: Has the thief been caught by the police?
Had the thief been caught by the police?
Had the thief caught by the police?
Was the thief caught by the police?
explain: Past perfect interrogative passive: Had + new subject + been + V3.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: 'He has not paid the bill.'
options: The bill has not been paid by him.
The bill not has been paid by him.
The bill has been not paid by him.
The bill had not been paid by him.
explain: 'Not' follows the first auxiliary: has not been paid.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "You should obey your elders."
options: Elders should obeyed by you.
Elders should be obey by you.
Elders should been obeyed by you.
Elders should be obeyed by you.
explain: Passive with a modal = modal + be + past participle.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "They could have saved him."
options: He could have been saved by them.
He could be saved by them.
He could been saved by them.
He could have saved by them.
explain: Perfect modals become modal + have been + V₃.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Can you finish this work today?"
options: Can this work finished by you today?
Can this work be finished by you today?
Could this work be finished by you today?
Can this work been finished by you today?
explain: The modal stays first; the object becomes subject, then be + V₃.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "You ought to help the poor."
options: The poor ought to helped by you.
The poor are ought to be helped by you.
The poor ought to be helped by you.
The poor ought to being helped by you.
explain: Semi-modal ought to is followed by be + V₃ in the passive.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "He has to finish the work."
options: The work have to be finished by him.
The work has to finished by him.
The work has to be finished by him.
The work is to been finished by him.
explain: Has to stays and agrees with singular "work"; then be + V₃.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Who can solve this problem?"
formula: By whom + modal + subject + be + V₃
options: By whom can this problem be solved?
By whom this problem can be solved?
Who can this problem be solved?
By whom can be this problem solved?
explain: "Who" becomes "By whom" and the modal is placed before the new subject.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Why did you break the window?"
options: Why did the window break by you?
Why the window is broken by you?
Why was the window broken by you?
Why the window was broken by you?
explain: Keep 'Why', then was + new subject + past participle + by agent.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Do you know him?" (Standard form)
options: Is he known to you?
Is he knowing to you?
Does he be known to you?
Was he known by you?
explain: 'Know' takes 'to' as the agent preposition: 'Is he known to you?'

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "Has anyone seen the thief?"
options: Has the thief been seen by anyone?
Was the thief seen by anyone?
Have the thief been seen by anyone?
Has the thief seen by anyone?
explain: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + V3; subject 'thief' is singular.

subject: English
prompt: Passive of: "What are you doing?"
options: What was being done by you?
What is being done by you?
What does being done by you?
What is done by you?
explain: Present continuous passive: is/are + being + V3; 'What' is the subject.

subject: English
prompt: Correct passive of 'People look up to him':
options: He is looked by people up to.
He is looked up by people to.
He is looked to up by people.
He is looked up to by people.
explain: In a prepositional/phrasal verb, the preposition stays with the verb in the passive: looked up to.

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence has no standard passive form?
options: They were playing cricket.
They had been playing cricket.
They will have played cricket.
They had played cricket.
explain: Past perfect continuous has no passive; 'had been being played' is not used.

subject: English
prompt: He said to me, "I am tired." Correct reporting verb in indirect speech is:
options: asked me
said me
told me
ordered me
explain: In assertive sentences, 'said to' becomes 'told' (with the object) and 'that' is added.

subject: English
prompt: She said to him, "Where are you going?" 'said to' changes to:
options: told him
asked him
said him
ordered him
explain: For interrogative sentences, 'said to' becomes 'asked' (or enquired).

subject: English
prompt: He said to me, "Please lend me your pen." Best reporting verb:
options: ordered me
exclaimed to me
requested me
told me that
explain: A polite 'please' request makes 'said to' become 'requested' (or begged).

subject: English
prompt: He said to us, "Let us go for a walk." Reporting verb becomes:
options: suggested that we should
ordered us to
told us that we
asked us if we
explain: 'Let us' expresses a proposal, so the reporting verb is 'suggested' or 'proposed'.

subject: English
prompt: He says, "I am ill." Correct indirect speech:
formula: Present reporting verb → no tense change
options: He says that he was ill.
He says that I am ill.
He said that he is ill.
He says that he is ill.
explain: A present-tense reporting verb leaves the tense unchanged; only the pronoun changes.

subject: English
topic: Tense Backshift Rules in Indirect Speech
prompt: Reporting verb in past: direct 'present perfect' (has/have + V3) changes to which tense?
options: Past perfect
Past perfect continuous
Simple past
Present perfect (unchanged)
explain: After a past reporting verb, present perfect backshifts to past perfect.

subject: English
topic: Tense Backshift Rules in Indirect Speech
prompt: He said, "I write letters." Correct indirect form: He said that he ___ letters.
options: had written
wrote
writes
was written
explain: Simple present becomes simple past after a past reporting verb.

subject: English
topic: Tense Backshift Rules in Indirect Speech
prompt: In indirect speech, a simple past verb in the quoted words normally changes to:
options: Past perfect
Past continuous
Present perfect
Simple present
explain: Simple past backshifts to past perfect (had + V3).

subject: English
topic: Tense Backshift Rules in Indirect Speech
prompt: Past continuous 'was/were doing' in direct speech becomes what after a past reporting verb?
options: had been doing
was done
had done
would be doing
explain: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous.

subject: English
topic: Tense Backshift Rules in Indirect Speech
prompt: Which modal usually stays unchanged in indirect speech after a past reporting verb?
options: ought to
will
can
shall
explain: Ought to, should, would, could, might do not backshift; can, will, shall, may do.

subject: English
prompt: He said, "Akbar was born in 1542." The usual reported form of the historical fact is:
options: He said that Akbar was born in 1542.
He said that Akbar had been being born in 1542.
He said that Akbar would be born in 1542.
He said that Akbar is born in 1542.
explain: A historical fact is reported without backshift, so the simple past stays as it is.

subject: English
prompt: Direct: He said, "The train had left before I reached." In indirect speech the verb "had left" will:
options: Remain had left
Become has left
Become left
Become had had left
explain: Past perfect cannot be shifted further back, so it stays unchanged.

subject: English
prompt: In reported speech, a first-person pronoun in the quoted words changes according to which word?
options: Subject of the reported clause
Object of the reporting verb
It does not change
Subject of the reporting verb
explain: First person (I, my, we) follows the subject of the reporting verb.

subject: English
prompt: In reported speech, a second-person pronoun (you, your) changes according to which word?
options: Tense of the reporting verb
Subject of the reporting verb
Object of the reporting verb
It never changes
explain: Second person (you, your) follows the object of the reporting verb.

subject: English
prompt: Rita said to Anu, "He is your friend." Which pronoun rule applies to "He" when reporting?
options: It changes to they
It changes to she
It changes to the reporter's person
It remains unchanged
explain: Third-person pronouns (he, she, they, it) do not change in reported speech.

subject: English
prompt: Mohan said to Sita, "You have lost my pen." Choose the correct indirect form.
options: Mohan told Sita that she had lost his pen
Mohan told Sita that she had lost her pen
Mohan told Sita that I had lost his pen
Mohan told Sita that he had lost his pen
explain: You → Sita (she); my → Mohan (his).

subject: English
prompt: She said to me, "I like you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
options: She told me that she liked me
She told me that I liked you
She told me that she liked you
She told me that I liked her
explain: I → she (subject of reporting verb); you → me (object).

subject: English
prompt: In indirect speech, 'tomorrow' (with a past reporting verb) normally changes to:
formula: tomorrow → the next day / the following day
options: that day
the next day
the day before
the previous day
explain: 'Tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day' after a past reporting verb.

subject: English
prompt: In indirect speech, 'yesterday' normally changes to:
formula: yesterday → the previous day / the day before
options: the next day
the day before
that day
the following day
explain: 'Yesterday' becomes 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

subject: English
prompt: In indirect speech, the word 'ago' (as in 'two years ago') changes to:
options: after
before
since
later
explain: 'Ago' becomes 'before', e.g. 'two years before'.

subject: English
prompt: In indirect speech, the demonstrative 'these' (as in 'these books') changes to:
options: that
them
those
there
explain: Near demonstratives shift to distant ones: this → that, these → those.

subject: English
prompt: Time and place words need NOT change when the speech is reported:
options: only when the speech is a question
only with a past reporting verb
at the same time and place as the speech
only in the passive voice
explain: If the report is made at the same time and place, words like 'here' and 'today' stay unchanged.

subject: English
prompt: A reported yes/no question is introduced by which linker?
options: that
no linker, only a comma
what or which
if or whether
explain: Yes/no questions have no wh-word, so indirect speech uses 'if' or 'whether'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct report: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.
He asked me that where I lived.
explain: Reported questions use statement word order: no auxiliary 'do', no 'that', and the verb is backshifted.

subject: English
prompt: "Will you come tomorrow?" she asked him. Report it.
options: that he would come the next day
if he will come tomorrow
if would he come the next day
if he would come the next day
explain: will→would, tomorrow→the next day, and 'if' is used with statement order.

subject: English
prompt: He asks me, "What are you reading?" Report it.
options: what I had been reading
what I am reading
what I was reading
what was I reading
explain: If the reporting verb is in the present tense, the tense does not change; only the pronoun does.

subject: English
prompt: "Why did you come here yesterday?" he asked me. Choose the correct part of the report.
options: why did I come there the day before
why I had come there the previous day
why I had come here the next day
why I came here yesterday
explain: Past simple→past perfect, here→there, yesterday→the previous day; statement order.

subject: English
prompt: "Shall we go now?" they asked. They asked whether ___ go then.
options: we should
they shall
they should
should they
explain: 'Shall' backshifts to 'should'. The pronoun changes to 'they', and the word order is that of a statement.

subject: English
prompt: Which reported question is ungrammatical?
options: He asked whether I would go or not.
He asked if I would go.
He asked whether or not I would go.
He asked if or not I would go.
explain: 'Or not' cannot follow 'if' directly in that position; 'whether or not' is the correct form.

subject: English
prompt: Report: The teacher said to the boy, "Stand up."
options: The teacher ordered the boy that stand up.
The teacher said the boy to stand up.
The teacher ordered the boy to stand up.
The teacher asked the boy if he stood up.
explain: An imperative is reported with ordered/commanded + object + to-infinitive; 'that' is not used.

subject: English
prompt: Report: She said to him, "Don't make noise."
options: She told him do not make noise.
She told him not to make noise.
She said him not to make noise.
She told him that not make noise.
explain: A negative command becomes 'not to + verb' after told/ordered; the 'don't' form is dropped.

subject: English
prompt: Best reporting verb: The doctor said to him, "You should quit smoking."
options: ordered
begged
forbade
advised
explain: 'Should/ought to' signals advice, so the reporting verb is advised/urged.

subject: English
prompt: Report: He said to her, "Pray, forgive me."
options: He ordered her to forgive him.
He advised her to forgive him.
He begged her to forgive him.
He warned her to forgive him.
explain: 'Pray' marks an earnest plea, so begged/implored/entreated is used.

subject: English
prompt: Indirect form of: She said to me, "May you live long!"
options: She exclaimed that I would have lived long.
She prayed that I might live long.
She asked me that I may live long.
She said to me that you might live long.
explain: A 'May…' wish becomes 'prayed/wished that' with 'might'; 'you' changes to 'I' (the listener).

subject: English
prompt: Indirect form of: He said, "What a fine day!"
options: He said that what a fine day it is.
He exclaimed that it was a very fine day.
He exclaimed that it had been a fine day.
He asked what a fine day it was.
explain: 'What a/How' is dropped; the exclamation becomes an assertive clause with 'very', introduced by 'exclaimed that'.

subject: English
prompt: Passive voice of: "Let us help the poor."
formula: Let + object + be + V3 (+ by agent)
options: The poor are let to be helped by us.
Let us be helped by the poor.
Let the poor helped by us.
Let the poor be helped by us.
explain: 'Let + object + V1' becomes 'Let + object + be + V3 + by agent'.

subject: English
prompt: Passive voice of: "Never tease animals."
options: Let never animals teased.
Let animals never be teased.
Let animals be never tease.
Animals are never let to be teased.
explain: Negative imperative: Let + object + never + be + V3.

subject: English
prompt: Passive voice of: "Do not laugh at the poor."
options: Let not the poor be laughed.
Let not the poor be laughed at.
Let the poor not laugh at.
Let not the poor laughed at.
explain: The preposition 'at' is retained: Let not the poor be laughed at.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct passive of the imperative: "Let me go."
formula: Let + object + be allowed to + V1
options: Let me be gone.
Let go be done by me.
I am let to go.
Let me be allowed to go.
explain: Intransitive 'go' has no object, so 'Let me go' becomes 'Let me be allowed to go.'

subject: English
prompt: Passive of 'He bought me a watch' with the direct object 'watch' as subject:
options: A watch had been bought for me by him.
A watch was bought to me by him.
A watch was bought for me by him.
A watch was bought me by him.
explain: With the direct object as subject, 'buy' needs 'for' before the indirect object (for me).

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence cannot normally be turned into the passive voice?
options: She resembles her mother.
She will meet her mother.
She has praised her mother.
She admires her mother.
explain: 'Resemble' is a stative verb, like 'have' for possession, and takes no passive.

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence normally has no passive form?
options: She has bought a big house.
She is building a big house.
She will build a big house.
She has a big house.
explain: 'Has' showing possession is stative and takes no passive; the other verbs are ordinary transitive actions.

subject: English
prompt: He said to us, "Beware of pickpockets." Best reporting verb in indirect speech:
options: warned us
asked us
wished us
told us that
explain: 'Beware' signals a caution, so 'said to' becomes 'warned': He warned us to beware of pickpockets.

subject: English
prompt: He said, "I used to play hockey." Choose the correct indirect speech.
options: He said that he had been used to playing hockey.
He said that he was used to play hockey.
He said that he had used to play hockey.
He said that he used to play hockey.
explain: "Used to" does not change in reported speech, as with other unchanging past habits.

subject: English
prompt: He said, "If I were you, I would apologise." Indirect speech of the verb forms is:
options: he would apologise, if he were me
he would have apologised
if he had been me, he would apologise
if he were me, he would apologise
explain: Unreal 'were/would' in a conditional stays unchanged; only pronouns change.
